categories.main_business_segments: Constellation Brands operates three business segments: Beer, Wine and Spirits, and Corporate Operations and Other. The Beer segment focuses on high-end imported Mexican beer brands and alternative beverage alcohol (ABA) products, including Corona Extra, Modelo Especial, and Pacifico. The Wine and Spirits segment includes higher-end wine brands such as Robert Mondavi Winery, Kim Crawford, Meiomi, and The Prisoner Wine Company, along with spirits brands like Casa Noble, High West, and SVEDKA. The company is the second-largest beer company in the U.S. and a major higher-end wine and spirits producer.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company operates breweries in Mexico (Nava and Obregon) with approximately 48 million hectoliters of capacity as of February 2024, expanding to 65 million hectoliters by 2028. Beer production utilizes water, agricultural products (yeast, grains, malt, hops), and packaging materials (glass, aluminum, cardboard). Wine production involves traditional fermentation and aging processes using grapes from owned vineyards and independent growers. The company operates 12 U.S. wineries, 2 in New Zealand, and 5 in Italy. Spirits production includes five distilleries in the U.S. for whiskey, brandy, bourbon, and ready-to-drink cocktails. A joint venture glass production plant in Nava supplies approximately 60% of glass bottle requirements.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The primary market is the United States, where the company sells through wholesale distributors, retailers, and government agencies. Products are distributed through separate networks for beer and wine/spirits portfolios. The company also sells in Canada, New Zealand, and other major world markets. Key customer types include wholesale distributors (with one major wholesaler representing approximately one-quarter of consolidated net sales for beer), retailers, on-premise locations, and direct-to-consumer channels. The company serves consumers across imported beer, alternative beverage alcohol, and premium wine and spirits categories.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in the United States, which is its largest market. International operations include production facilities in Mexico (breweries in Nava and Obregon), New Zealand (two wineries), and Italy (five wineries). The company has vineyard holdings in California, Oregon, New Zealand, and Italy. As of February 2024, the company owned or leased approximately 18,200 acres of vineyards globally. Employees are located in various countries, with approximately 10,600 total employees including those from a joint venture. The company sources grapes from approximately 430 independent growers in the U.S. and 40 in New Zealand and Italy.
categories.supply_chain_position: Constellation Brands operates across multiple points in the beverage alcohol supply chain. In beer, the company is primarily a producer and marketer, operating breweries and relying on suppliers for raw materials and packaging. The company has backward integration through ownership of vineyards and a joint venture glass production plant. In wine and spirits, the company produces, ages, and markets products. The company operates in the midstream to downstream segments, with significant control over production and distribution through its own facilities and wholesale distributor networks, while also expanding into direct-to-consumer channels.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company's strategic priorities include: (1) building strong brands through advantaged routes to market; (2) developing a consumer-obsessed culture with robust innovation capabilities; (3) deploying capital through disciplined and balanced priorities; (4) delivering impactful ESG initiatives; and (5) achieving best-in-class operational efficiency. R&D focuses on consumer-led premiumization and innovation, including new product launches like Modelo Oro, Modelo Chelada variants, Corona Non-Alcoholic, and Corona Sunbrew. The company is investing in Digital Business Acceleration initiatives to enhance technology capabilities in procurement, supply chain planning, and logistics. ESG targets include water restoration, GHG emissions reduction, zero waste certification, and circular packaging enhancements.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through product sales of beer, wine, and spirits. Beer segment revenue comes from sales of Mexican beer brands and alternative beverages through wholesale distributors and retailers. Wine and Spirits segment revenue comes from sales of wine and spirits brands through multiple channels including U.S. wholesale distribution (approximately 70% through Southern Glazer's Wine and Spirits), direct-to-consumer channels, 3-tier eCommerce, and international markets. The company also generates revenue through hospitality locations (tasting rooms and tap rooms). Fiscal 2024 net sales were $9,961.8 million, with Beer representing $8,162.6 million and Wine and Spirits representing $1,799.2 million.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In beer, the company competes with Anheuser-Busch InBev, The Boston Beer Company, Heineken, Mark Anthony, and Molson Coors. The company is the second-largest beer company in the U.S. and the #1 share gainer in the high-end beer segment. Modelo Especial became the #1 beer brand in the U.S. in dollar sales in Fiscal 2024. In wine, competitors include Deutsch Family Wine & Spirits, Duckhorn Portfolio, E. & J. Gallo Winery, Ste. Michelle Wine Estates, Treasury Wine Estates, and Trinchero Family Estates. In spirits, competitors include Bacardi USA, Beam Suntory, Brown-Forman, Diageo, and Pernod Ricard. The company competes on quality, price, brand recognition, reputation, and distribution strength.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Constellation Brands is a large-cap company with fiscal 2024 net sales of $9,961.8 million, representing 5% growth from fiscal 2023 net sales of $9,452.6 million. Operating income increased 11% to $3,169.7 million in fiscal 2024 from $2,842.9 million in fiscal 2023. Net income attributable to CBI was $1,727.4 million in fiscal 2024 compared to a loss of $(71.0) million in fiscal 2023. The company has a market capitalization of approximately $42.0 billion as of the last business day of the most recently completed second fiscal quarter. The company is classified as a large accelerated filer and is one of the fastest-growing large CPG companies in the U.S. at retail.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The company's value proposition centers on powerful, consumer-connected, high-quality brands that deliver premiumization and innovation. Key differentiators include: (1) leadership in the high-end beer segment with iconic Mexican beer brands (Corona Extra, Modelo Especial); (2) a portfolio reshaped toward higher-margin, higher-growth wine and spirits brands; (3) consumer-led innovation addressing premiumization and betterment trends; (4) omni-channel distribution capabilities including DTC, 3-tier eCommerce, and international expansion; (5) operational excellence through cost savings initiatives and supply chain optimization; and (6) commitment to ESG and responsible beverage alcohol consumption. The company emphasizes building brands people love and elevating human connections as core to its mission.
